methodological_rigor.justification: Large-scale observational study of 20,005 brain tumor patients from 78 hospitals across Germany. Appropriate statistical methods including generalized linear mixed models with hospitals as random factor, chi-square tests, ANOVA, logistic GLMMs for treatment/outcome proportions. Confidence intervals and odds ratios reported with p<0.05 significance threshold. Limitations acknowledged including retrospective administrative data, potential coding errors, missing tumor grading and functional status data. Well-designed mixed model approach accounts for hospital clustering.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Real-world evidence on trends in brain tumor care and neurosurgical management across different age groups in a large, nationally representative German cohort. Directly relevant to clinical practice during pandemic years. Provides insights into comorbidity profiles, frailty trends, and surgical rates by age group. LoE elevated by large sample size and nationwide representation, though observational design and lack of causal inference limit clinical impact.

reporting_quality.justification: Clear description of study setting, data collection methods with specific ICD-10 and OPS coding systems, and detailed statistical approaches with model specifications. Results presented with confidence intervals and odds ratios with appropriate tables and figures. However, no explicit STROBE checklist adherence statement provided. Data and code availability not mentioned. Administrative data limitations acknowledged but not fully detailed.

novelty_literature.justification: First granular analysis of age-stratified trends in brain tumor care during pandemic period in a large nationwide cohort. Extends prior work by authors from 2023 with more detailed subgroup analyses. Notable finding of 75-84 year age group deviating from overall trends. Incremental contribution to pandemic-era observational literature on neurosurgical practice. Limited mechanistic novelty but useful real-world descriptive data.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections. Effective presentation of findings across multiple age brackets with appropriate tables and figures showing trends over time. Discussion thoughtfully addresses potential mechanisms including COVID-19 hesitancy, admission thresholds, and selective surgical decision-making. Appropriate acknowledgment of limitations and inability to establish causality. Publication-ready quality.

key_strengths: Large-scale nationwide observational cohort with 20,005 patients from 78 German hospitals, providing robust real-world evidence on pandemic-era brain tumor care trends
Rigorous statistical approach using generalized linear mixed models with hospitals as random factor, appropriately accounting for clustering and institutional variation
Granular age-stratified analysis revealing distinct patterns, notably the anomalous 75-84 year age group that diverged from overall improvement trends
Comprehensive assessment of both patient characteristics (comorbidity via Elixhauser Index, frailty via Hospital Frailty Risk Score) and management outcomes (resection rates, ICU transfer, mortality)
Well-reasoned discussion of potential mechanisms including pandemic-related admission hesitancy, selective surgical decision-making, and improved frailty profiles
key_concerns: Retrospective administrative data subject to coding errors and missing clinically important variables (tumor grading, functional status, long-term outcomes)
Cannot establish causal relationships from observational design; changes may reflect selection effects rather than true improvements in care
Data and code availability not addressed; no explicit STROBE adherence stated despite observational study design
Limited generalizability to non-German healthcare systems with different hospital capacity, pandemic response, and treatment protocols
Analysis cannot differentiate whether improvements result from better care quality versus patient selection/triage effects during pandemic
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid real-world observational study with appropriate statistical methods and large sample size. Suitable for Tier 3 journals (BMC Cancer, Current Oncology, European Journal of Cancer) given descriptive value for pandemic-era neurosurgical trends but limited causal insight and methodological novelty. No mechanistic advances or practice-changing recommendations emerge from findings.
